extraction.name: Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges
extraction.description: A review paper critically examining the current state of Visual Question Answering (VQA), including problem formulation, existing datasets (DAQUAR, COCO-QA, The VQA Dataset, FM-IQA, Visual7W, Visual Genome, SHAPES), evaluation metrics, and algorithms. It discusses limitations, biases, and future directions for VQA and image understanding research.
extraction.creator: Kushal Kaife and Christopher Kanan
extraction.citeAs: Kaife, K., & Kanan, C. (2017). Visual Question Answering: Datasets, Algorithms, and Future Challenges. arXiv preprint arXiv:1610.01465.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The paper reviews multiple datasets with different collection methods. DAQUAR uses images from NYU-DepthV2. COCO-QA uses an NLP algorithm to derive QA pairs from COCO image captions. The VQA Dataset (COCO-VQA and SYNTH-VQA) uses Amazon Mechanical Turk workers to generate questions and answers. FM-IQA uses human-generated questions and answers. Visual Genome and Visual7W use crowdsourced annotators via free-form and region-specific prompting. SHAPES uses synthetic shapes.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from NYU-DepthV2, Microsoft Common Objects in Context (COCO), Flickr100M, and synthetic cartoon imagery. Textual questions and answers generated by humans or NLP algorithms.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For COCO-VQA, Amazon Mechanical Turk workers generated questions to 'stump a smart robot' and separate workers generated answers (10 per question). For Visual Genome, annotators used free-form and region-specific prompting. For COCO-QA, an NLP algorithm derived questions from captions. For DAQUAR, ground truth was collected manually.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Inter-human agreement on COCO-VQA is about 83.3%. There is significant disagreement on 'Why' questions and subjective questions. The dataset contains biases where language alone can predict answers with high accuracy.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 10 answers per question for The VQA Dataset; 5 answers per question for DAQUAR-consensus; 17 QA pairs per image for Visual Genome.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Amazon Mechanical Turk workers; human annotators for Visual Genome and DAQUAR.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: NLP algorithm for COCO-QA; VGGNet, ResNet, GoogLeNet, LSTM, MCB, etc. for algorithmic evaluation (not annotation).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: VQA can aid blind and visually impaired individuals by providing information about images. It improves human-computer interaction and image retrieval. It serves as a component of a Turing Test for image understanding.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Strong language biases in datasets like COCO-VQA allow algorithms to answer correctly without looking at images. Biases in question phrasing and answer distribution (e.g., 'yes' is more common). Synthetic datasets (SYNTH-VQA, SHAPES) were created to reduce these biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Existing datasets are too small to train complex models. They contain grammatical errors, subjective questions, and biases that inflate performance metrics. Evaluation metrics like WUPS and Accuracy_VQA have limitations in handling semantic similarity and multi-word answers. Many datasets lack diversity in question types or have long-tailed answer distributions.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training and evaluating Visual Question Answering algorithms. Benchmarking computer vision and natural language processing systems. Research into image understanding and reasoning.
